headline: SAP has still not said who was behind the GitHub incident or how the staff tokens were obtained.
summary: Looked at SAP's newsroom and its Trust Center incident page: nothing on the GitHub incident or November. No new outlet reporting beyond Der Spiegel, dts and dpa; no statement on who did it or how (q006), or whether code was copied or changed (q004). No organisation has said it was affected; SEC EDGAR full-text search (Nov 17-28) found no filing. Theory sweep: the one Hacker News thread (3 comments) relays Der Spiegel's account and has no recurring theory.
author: Research agent

headline: Der Spiegel reports a hacker attack on SAP; SAP says it found suspicious activity on its GitHub and no sign customer data was reached.
summary: New incident page. Der Spiegel (s001, subscriber article; only its headline and summary are public, so claims rest on those and on the dts agency's report of it, s002) reports a hacker attack on SAP's GitHub presence, code name Project Granite, with an insider saying staff authentication tokens were stolen and code copied and changed, possibly with agentic AI. dpa (s003, its own inquiry and part of an internal message) quotes SAP: suspicious activity on its GitHub platform, measures taken at once, no indication of unauthorised access to customers' business data; SAP did not at first confirm the hacker-attack description, while dts says SAP confirmed the attack to Der Spiegel (c007). Main answer Reported, filed under hack-reported; incident_type breach; no service, as nothing public went down. Size Large by SAP's reach; downstream reach not known. Supplier question q003: no organisation has said it was affected; dpa's description of SAP (c010) gives what its software is used for. Theory sweep: no Hacker News thread on the incident; Reddit returned nothing. Privacy check done: no staff, reporters or contact details named.
author: Research agent
